subject: Regional failover credits & pricing ask — EU availability tiers
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acmecloud.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick question on failover SLA credits across regions

Hi Chloe,

Quick note after the demo — thanks for walking us through Dedicated and the prefilling cache behavior. One thing we hadn't fully scoped: our compliance team requires explicit regional failover guarantees for EU customers. Specifically, they want clarity on how credits would apply if EU capacity fails and traffic routes to a US region.

Can you share how Redwood calculates uptime credits in cross-region failover events, and whether we can get a blended-price/discount if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool? Also, are there lower-latency response guarantees you can lock for EU instances if we opt for a 99.95% band vs 99.9%?

Appreciate a concise table and an example calculation (preferably with our anticipated 5M tokens/month).

Cheers,
Liam
Senior Infrastructure PM
Acme Cloud

Attachment: N/A

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acmecloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick question on failover SLA credits across regions

Hi Liam — thanks for the thoughtful questions and for the detail on volume. Short answer: yes, we can both: (1) provide explicit cross-region failover crediting rules and (2) offer a blended reserved pricing path for a 12-month commit. Below is a concise breakdown; I'll attach the full pricing grid and a worked example.

Summary table (high-level):
- 99.9% (Standard): 4-hour P1 response window; credits = 5% month bill per 0.5% below SLO; regional failover treated as an incident if the primary EU pool falls below SLO.
- 99.95% (Priority): 2-hour P1 response window; credits = 7.5% month bill per 0.25% below SLO; capacity priority during failover + warm standby reservation option.
- Cross-region failover: if traffic is routed to a non-EU region as a Redwood-managed fallback, we apply pro-rata credits to the affected EU usage and a 50% mitigated-credit to reflect reduced latency SLA mismatch. Example below.

Proposal for 12-month reserved pool (5M tokens/mo baseline):
- Commit discount: 18% on per-token hosted rates for Dedicated EU pools.
- Add-on: Warm standby (reserved warm capacity in designated backup region) at +6% of committed spend — reduces credit multiplier and guarantees faster cold-start ramps.
- Pricing example (worked): see attached failover-pricing-sheet.xlsx.

I've attached the SLA-Pricing-Grid.pdf and the worked spreadsheet. Ben and Karthik are on-thread for commercial and technical alignment. If you want, we can sketch a mutual action plan this week.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Exec, EU Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-Pricing-Grid.pdf, failover-pricing-sheet.xlsx

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 12:01:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: counter thresholds & approval for blended discount

Chloe / Karthik — quick internal note before we go further with Acme: procurement will want a clean formula for credits and a simple fallback pricing line item (warm standby). I suggest we offer a commercial concession path:
- Base commit (12mo, 5M tokens/mo): 18%
- If Acme signs a 24mo with auto-true-up: +4% (total 22%)
- One-time implementation credit for migration/testing (applied to month 1): $12,000
- We treat warm standby as an opt-in SKU; if they accept, reduce cross-region credit mitigation from 50% to 25%.

Are we comfortable with that approval band? Vanessa, can you confirm finance OKs the $12k migration credit as a one-off for this deal size?

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Sales Strategy

Attachment: SLA-terms-acme-draft.docx

Thanks Chloe — the table helps a lot. A couple of follow ups from procurement: (1) they want the credit math formalized in the contract (we'll need DocuSign-ready language), and (2) is the warm standby billing model monthly amortized or invoiced up-front? For budgeting they'd prefer amortized monthly.

Also — will the reduced credit mitigation (25%) if we take warm standby be written into the SLA as a separate clause? Procurement flags that we need deterministic credit triggers, e.g., how you define "primary EU pool falls below SLO" in telemetry terms.

If you can get a DocuSign link with contract language and an update to the pricing spreadsheet showing amortized monthly for warm standby, we can take this to final legal review.

Appreciate it,
Liam

Liam — perfect, we'll get a DocuSign-ready draft and an updated spreadsheet with amortized warm-standby billing to you by end of day Friday. Quick clarifications we will include in the contract language and telemetry appendix:

- "Primary EU pool" definition: the active capacity pool serving >50% of EU-tagged traffic for the account, as measured by our routing telemetry aggregated on 5-minute buckets.
- "Credit trigger": sustained SLO breach defined as more than 3 consecutive 5-minute buckets below target for a 30-minute rolling window.
- "Cross-region calculation": credits applied to the pro-rated EU-flagged usage in the affected billing period; mitigation factor (25% w/ warm standby) reduces the credit applied to reflect reserved capacity.
- "Warm standby billing": amortized monthly over the term unless Acme elects an upfront prepayment (we will show both numbers).

Ben / Vanessa — please confirm the $12k one-time migration credit and the 22% max commit discount path if Acme goes 24 months. Once you confirm I will attach the DocuSign and ping Acme procurement.

Best,
Chloe
Senior Account Exec, EU Sales
Redwood Inference
